newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Shell says Black Sea oil talks proceeding well.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Black Sea oil talks proceeding well.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group, a potential investor in Ukraine's oil and gas sector, said on Wednesday that it was making progress in its latest round of talks to explore Black Sea oil reserves.
"We have people down here in Simferopol talking with Chernomorneftegaz, and discussions are going very well," Les Lastowecki, executive director of Shell's Ukrainian unit Shell Pecten, told Reuters.

Shell Pecten and Ukraine's Crimea-based Chernomorneftegaz company, responsible for exploration and production, are forming a joint venture to drill for offshore oil after Shell won a tender last autumn to explore four blocks on the sea's shelf.
Interfax Ukraine news agency this week quoted a top State Oil and Gas Committee official as saying that a deal would be delayed until Ukraine passed new tax laws early this year.
But Lastowecki said tax laws would have no bearing on talks. "We're discussing production-sharing concepts, including taxation...Talks are progressing very well at this stage."

Although Ukrainian officials said last year the company was considering investing up to $1 billion in natural gas pipeline and oil drilling projects in the former Soviet republic, Lastowecki said investment levels would depend on findings.
"A lot depends on what we find," he said, adding that it was still unclear how much oil would be found there.
